title: Sprint 7 launch + method naming
notes: Launched Sprint 7 as the new active producer-identity program after Sprint 6's pairwise merge-only path failed to produce a trustworthy execution route. Locked the new method family as identity_dossier_select_v1 (Identity Dossier Select): reusable producer dossiers, shortlist generation, select-best-or-none adjudication, explicit RELATED_BUT_DISTINCT handling, AI-only escalation, and merges only from accepted SAME_AS edges. Human pair review at scale is out; budget remains fixed; abstention is preferred over risky merges.

title: Identity dossier schema + candidate inventory
notes: Defined producer_dossier_v1, source_signal_inventory, and edge_taxonomy_v1 as the durable evidence contract for Sprint 7. Locked the cheap dossier as backbone-first and regulatory-aware because the canonical producer table is still sparse for websites, aliases, importer links, history, and producer-level external IDs. Fixed the selector label set at SAME_AS, RELATED_BUT_DISTINCT, NONE, and UNSURE; only accepted SAME_AS edges are merge-eligible. The next session should design shortlist generation against that fixed dossier object.

title: Autonomous continuation gating
notes: Added an explicit Autonomous continuation yes/no field to the session handoff protocol and tightened the Auto Next Session heartbeat to rely on that field instead of inferring readiness from prose. The current setting remains blocked because the shortlist seed-source decision for importer, retailer, and profile sources is still unresolved.

title: Shortlist generation design
notes: Defined shortlist_generation_v1 as the fixed retrieval contract for Identity Dossier Select. Locked Tier A-only candidate seeding (canonical lexical, LWIN producer names, TTB brand/applicant names, and state-registration brand/legal names), demoted importer/retailer/profile sources to rerank or escalation only, capped the raw candidate union at 24 and the final selector shortlist at 12, and added suppression rules for weak fuzzy hits, permit-only adjacency, shared-surname/first-word collisions, and merchant/importer-context-only candidates. The autonomy blocker from Session 10.2a is now cleared; the next session should design the selector harness against this fixed shortlist contract.
